title: Giving Martin 1 Extra Pawn Until I LOSE
summary: Reverse odds vs Martin (250): the creator keeps his normal army and gives Martin a huge extra pawn army, starting at 23 pawns and adding more each game until Martin wins. He wins by pushing pawns, picking off blunders and promoting; Martin finally wins with 45 pawns after an early ...Bxf2/...g3 mating net, and then the creator beats 47 pawns.
rules: Player (White): standard army. Martin (Black): king + pieces plus extra pawns filling ranks 3-7 (23 pawns in game 1, ~47 in the last).
Add pawns to Martin after every player win; normal chess rules.
win_condition: Checkmate Martin; continue until Martin wins (he won at 45 pawns).

opponent.name: Martin
opponent.avatar_description: Cartoon bearded man with bushy eyebrows and a brown sweater (chess.com Martin style); remake as an original bearded-guy cartoon.

board.theme_notes: chess.com brown/cream board almost filled with black pawns.

setup: Game 1 example: Black back rank rnbqkbnr, pawns on all of ranks 7, 6 and part of 5 (23 pawns total); White standard. Pawn count rises each game (~+2-5) up to 47.
events: Pawn count increases after each win (counter).
current_impl_issues: Legacy 'gift' starts at 1 extra pawn (+1 per win); video starts Martin at 23 pawns and climbs to 45-47. Start count should be ~23 and step larger.
evidence: SRT 0:00 'giving Martin as many pawns as he needs to beat me we'll start with 23 pawns and add some each game'; 17:40 'give him two more pawns... maximum Pawn power'; 18:00 'Checkmate... it took Martin technically 45 pawns... ultimately it took him 47 pawns'.
